- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast rise to 3–4% after spike.
- Forecast mean reverts too slowly; if 3+ consecutive days show downward trend, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until trend flattens.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings, model tends to lag by 1–2 days — adjust forecast to match sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses early “rebound” phases after sharp drops — add 1–2% buffer if sentiment turns positive after drop.
